sections.h2: How does selling a house in Madison Heights, MI work?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer, and every route finishes with a deed recorded in Oakland County and a transfer affidavit filed with the city. The route you pick mostly changes how long the middle takes and who carries the repair bill.

Madison Heights had 28,297 residents on the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate, a dip of 0.6% from the April 2020 base. Those people fit into 7.09 square miles, about 4,018 per square mile. Between 2020 and 2024 the city counted 13,620 households, 64.8% of them owner-occupied, with a median owner-occupied value of $199,100 and median gross rent of $1,176.

Mean travel time to work is 25.3 minutes, and 18.8% of residents are 65 or older. With a population that size spread over older streets, the questions sellers raise most are about condition, tenants and the tax bill that follows the house to its next owner.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Madison Heights for a home seller?
sections.html:
Madison Heights is a fully built-out inner-ring suburb of Detroit, roughly 12 miles north of downtown, in Oakland County. Residents voted to incorporate it as a city on January 17, 1955, after it had been part of Royal Oak Township.

Troy sits to the north, Royal Oak to the west, Hazel Park to the south and Warren to the east. Dequindre Road on the east side is also the Oakland and Macomb county line. Interstate 75 runs north to south along the west side, and Interstate 696 forms much of the southern edge. The city counts more than 112 miles of road and maintains 105 of them.

About 91% of the buildings are single-family homes or condominiums, which works out to roughly 9,800 residential owners, while about 60% of the tax base comes from light industrial and commercial property. That mix is why the city sits inside Oakland County's Automation Alley.

  • Public schools: Madison District Public Schools and Lamphere Public Schools both serve addresses in the city.
  • Other schools: Bishop Foley Catholic High School is private, and Four Corners Montessori Academy is a public charter.
  • Local draws: 168 Asian Mart, a 38,000-square-foot store described as the largest Asian supermarket in southeast Michigan, and a Chinese cultural center are both in the city.
  • Education level: 90.4% of adults 25 and older finished high school and 33.9% hold a bachelor's degree or more.

sections.h2: Does Madison Heights require an inspection before I sell?
sections.html:
No. The city's own FAQ says Madison Heights does not require or provide resale inspections, so a seller does not need to book a city walk-through before a closing.

A house that someone else occupies is treated differently. Anyone who owns an occupied home in the city and does not live there is a landlord under the municipal code and needs a landlord license, even if no rent changes hands. A qualified relative living in the home gets the fees and inspection waived. A landlord without a license cannot collect rent or evict a tenant, which matters if you are carrying a tenant while the house is on the market.

Source: City of Madison Heights landlord licensing page. A first license can run less than three years with the fee prorated, and renewals run four years with a new inspection each time. Current taxes, special assessments and water bills must be paid before the city issues the license.

sections.h2: When are Madison Heights property taxes due, and what carries over at closing?
sections.html:
The city bills and collects the tax itself, with summer bills due by August 31 and winter bills due by February 17 before penalties start. Summer bills arrive the first week of July and winter bills the first week of December.

Miss the summer date and a 4% penalty lands on September 1, followed by 1/2% for each month after. Winter taxes unpaid after February 17 pick up 3% on February 18. City Hall takes payment through March 2, and from March 3 everything goes to the Oakland County Treasurer with added penalties.

The buyer's side of the bill changes after a sale. Under MCL 211.27a, the taxable value in the year after a transfer resets to the state equalized value, so a house held for decades under the annual cap can see a large jump for the new owner. Sellers who claimed the principal residence exemption must file a rescission with the local tax collecting unit within 90 days of moving out, and a missed filing carries a penalty of $5 per day up to $200 under MCL 211.7cc. The closing agent is required to hand both the buyer and seller the affidavit and rescission forms at the table.

sections.h2: What paperwork and recording costs come with a Madison Heights sale?
sections.html:
Expect a recorded deed, a tax certification for a warranty deed, transfer tax, and a property transfer affidavit. Most of it is routine when a title company handles the closing.

  • Recording: Oakland County's Register of Deeds records the deed. Documents need a 2.5 inch top margin and must be notarized. Hand-carried and title-company documents come back in about two weeks, mailed ones in two to four.
  • Tax certificate: a warranty deed must be certified at the county Treasurer's Office to show taxes are current, at $5.
  • Transfer tax: state tax is $3.75 per $500 of value and the county adds 55 cents per $500 where the county has fewer than 2,000,000 people. On a $200,000 sale that is $1,500 plus $220, or $1,720. Transfers to a child or grandchild are among the exemptions in MCL 207.526.
  • Transfer affidavit: it is due within 45 days of the transfer. The city fines $5 per day, capped at $200 for residential property, and the affidavit goes to the Assessing Department at 300 W Thirteen Mile Road.

Call the Oakland County Register of Deeds for the current recording fee before you mail a document. The office takes questions at 248-858-0597.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a Madison Heights house quickly?
sections.html:
Three routes exist, and the difference between them is mostly financing and condition. Compare them on the net you keep after repairs, carrying costs and closing fees, not on the headline price.

  • List with an agent: you get showings and market exposure, and the buyer's lender and appraisal set the pace.
  • Sell by owner: you keep control of price and terms, and you handle the disclosures, the paperwork and the buyer questions yourself.
  • Cash offer: a buyer purchases the house as it stands with no lender step, so a house that needs repairs, or one with a tenant in place, can still close.

If you want a number from us, send the address and we will make a cash offer on the house in its current condition. Whether you accept it is up to you.

faqs.q: Do I need a city inspection to sell my house in Madison Heights?
faqs.a: No. The city says it does not require or provide resale inspections. A landlord license and inspection apply only if someone other than you occupies the home.

faqs.q: What happens if I rent out my house without a Madison Heights landlord license?
faqs.a: You lose the right to collect rent or evict the tenant until you hold a license. The license is required for any occupied home you do not live in, even when you charge nothing, though a qualified relative living there waives the fee and the inspection.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a $200,000 sale in Madison Heights?
faqs.a: It comes to $1,720: $1,500 at the state rate of $3.75 per $500 and $220 at the county rate of 55 cents per $500. The deed must show the value or carry an affidavit that states it.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Madison Heights property taxes after March 2?
faqs.a: To the Oakland County Treasurer. City Hall accepts payment through March 2, and from March 3 the bill moves to the county with added penalties.

faqs.q: How soon must the property transfer affidavit be filed in Madison Heights?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the transfer. Late filers owe $5 per day up to $200 on a residential property, and the form goes to the city Assessing Department.
